newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel army demands Palestinians arrest officer.
newsitem.headline: Israel army demands Palestinians arrest officer.

text.p: Israel's army demanded on Wednesday the immediate arrest of a senior Palestinian police officer it suspects of directing other policemen to fire on an Israeli rabbi in the West Bank.
"Israeli security officials appealed...to their Palestinian colleagues and asked for the immediate arrest of Deputy Commander Jihad Masouni, a senior official in the Nablus police," the army said.
The Palestinian governor of Nablus rejected the demand.
On Monday the army said it had arrested three Palestinian policemen who were trying to attack Har Bracha, a Jewish settlement near the Palestinian-ruled city of Nablus in the West Bank.

On Wednesday the army said it suspected Masouni of directing members of the same group to carry out a shooting attack that damaged the car of Rabbi Yitzhak Levanon last Thursday near Elon Moreh settlement.
The army said another Palestinian officer had been arrested on suspicion of planning attacks near the West Bank Palestinian-ruled town of Tulkarm.
Mahmoud al-Alloul, Palestinian governor of Nablus, called the Israeli allegations "absolutely untrue".

"We asked them to hand the police back over. We will investigate the incident and take measures not according to the Israeli investigation but rather according to the Palestinian investigation," he told Reuters.
The Palestinian territories have been tense since Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem four months ago, sparking weeks of Palestinian unrest.

"The Palestinian police will have to do serious maintenance and answer for themselves all of the questions as to what the commanders of these police were doing, where the weapons came from, what's the level of supervision and control -- and to uproot this evil from within," Israel's central army commander, Major-General Uzi Dayan, told reporters.
